_comment: SUBLETS tracker — whole apartments only (no roommates/room shares), month-to-month, <=$2500, Cole's 9 Brooklyn neighborhoods. Runs off the same apt_watcher.py as config.json but with its own DB and ntfy topic so the two feeds never mix: python3 apt_watcher.py --config config.sublets.json --db seen_sublets.db
_comment_max_age: Tighter than the long-term tracker (14d): sublets get taken within days, so anything older than a week is almost certainly gone.

filters._comment_exclude_keywords: Room-share phrases that are safe as plain substrings. Anything containing the word 'room' lives in exclude_regex instead -- 'room for rent' as a substring also matches '1 bedROOM for rent', which would silently drop whole apartments.
filters._comment_exclude_regex: Two jobs. (1) Room shares whose phrasing collides with legitimate whole-apartment titles -- \b stops 'room for rent' from matching inside 'bedroom for rent', so '1 bedroom for rent' still gets through while 'Furnished room for rent' does not. (2) Sub-month stays: month-to-month means at least a month, so '9 Days:', 'two weeks', 'Oct 1 - 15' and weekly rates are all out. The day pattern stops at 27 so a '30 day notice' post survives.
filters._comment_prefer_keywords: NOT a filter — a highlight. Requiring 'month to month' in the title would drop most real listings, since plenty of open-ended sublets never use the phrase. Matches get a star in the push instead.
filters._comment_exclude_locations: Backstop for geo-circle bleed. Only fires when Craigslist affirmatively tags a hood that isn't on Cole's list — most sublet posts are tagged just 'Brooklyn' and pass through on the circle alone. Carroll Gardens is deliberately NOT here: it sits between Cobble Hill and Red Hook, so a listing tagged there is almost always on a wanted border.

_comment_sources: Empirically probed 2026-08-20. Craigslist's dedicated 'sub' (sublets & temporary) category is the workhorse. Leasebreak, FurnishedFinder and Flip all 403 — use their own alerts. Craigslist ?query= searches return a JS shell with zero parseable cards, so category browsing is the only thing that works.

sources.name: Sublets ≤$2.5k · Greenpoint / N-W Williamsburg
sources._note: Circle is tuned to sit north of the Williamsburg Bridge and west of the BQE; 'east/south williamsburg' tags are dropped as a backstop.

sources.name: Sublets ≤$2.5k · Brownstone Bklyn (Ft Greene/Bklyn Hts/Cobble/Boerum/Prospect Hts/Park Slope)
Sublets ≤$2.5k · Red Hook
sources._note: Red Hook falls ~1.6mi from the brownstone circle's center, outside its 1.4mi radius, so it needs its own.

sources.name: Sublet.com · Brooklyn
sources._note: Cards state unit type and term outright ('Apartment ... Month to Month' vs 'Room Rental ... Min 6 Months'), which the keyword filters read directly. Listing page is borough-wide, so the adapter pulls each neighborhood from the detail page and require_any_locations does the geo work. The page is ~750KB and genuinely slow, so the timeout is generous; a timeout just skips the source for that cycle.

sources.name: Listings Project · NYC sublets
sources._note: Heavily sublet-oriented and one of the few non-Craigslist sources that doesn't block us. Neighborhood and bed count come from the URL slug, so it needs an explicit location match.

sources.name: Reddit · r/NYCapartments
sources._note: Very high noise (mostly ISO posts) and rate-limits to 429 easily; fails gracefully when it does.

_comment_topic: Local copy carries the topic literally. The copy committed to the PUBLIC GitHub repo has this set to null instead -- an ntfy topic is a public URL, so anyone who reads it in a public repo can read your listings feed and push to it. In the cloud it comes from the NTFY_TOPIC env var, set from the NTFY_TOPIC_SUBLETS repo secret.
